ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, B, H, C are on the same straight line, A is above H, AH is perpendicular to BC; M is located on side AC, and BM and HM are also drawn in the figure. Reasoning: From the problem statement, BM is a median, so M is the midpoint of AC. Since AH is an altitude, AH ⟂ BC, and H is on BC, triangle AHC is right-angled at H, and AC is its hypotenuse. According to the theorem on the midpoint of the hypotenuse of a right triangle, the midpoint M of hypotenuse AC is equidistant from the three points A, H, C, so MH = MC = MA. Therefore, in triangle MHC, MH = MC, so it is an isosceles triangle. Also because CM is on CA and CH is on CB, ∠HCM is ∠ACB = 30°. The base angles of isosceles triangle MHC are equal, therefore ∠MHC = ∠HCM = 30°.

method.method_draft: Use the right-triangle midpoint theorem. From the diagram, note that H lies on BC with AH perpendicular BC, and M lies on AC. From the text, BM is a median, so M is the midpoint of AC. Since AH is an altitude, triangle AHC is right at H. In a right triangle, the midpoint of the hypotenuse is equidistant from all three vertices, so in triangle AHC, M satisfies MH = MC = MA. Therefore triangle MHC is isosceles with MH = MC. Because M is on AC and H is on BC, angle HCM equals angle ACB, which is 30 degrees. Hence the equal base angle angle MHC is also 30 degrees.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates. From the diagram, place H at the origin and HC on the positive x-axis. Since AH is an altitude, let A = (0, h), and choose C = (1, 0). From the text, angle C = 30 degrees, so in right triangle AHC, tan 30 degrees = AH/HC = h/1, giving h = 1/sqrt(3). Since BM is a median, M is the midpoint of AC, so M = (1/2, 1/(2sqrt(3))). The slope of HM is [1/(2sqrt(3))]/[1/2] = 1/sqrt(3), so the angle that HM makes with HC is arctan(1/sqrt(3)) = 30 degrees. Therefore angle MHC = 30 degrees.
